title: Gegenschein over ALMA
caption: Gegenschein and the Milky Way over ALMA, Chajnantor plateau, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at ALMA, Chajnantor plateau, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: On the right of this image, the arc of the Milky Way soars above ALMA, the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array, an observatory ESO is a partner in. On the arc to the left, however, a different glow, a faint brightening of the night sky, competes for attention.

That glow is gegenschein, German for "countershine". It sits along the ecliptic at the point directly opposite the Sun, and it arises when interplanetary dust in the outer Solar System, shed by comets and broken-up asteroids, scatters incoming sunlight.

Across most of the world, light pollution from artificial sources hides sights such as gegenschein and even the Milky Way. By some estimates, more than 80% of the world's population lives under light-polluted skies, which makes places like the Atacama Desert, home to ALMA, all the more special.

understand.summary: This is a ground-based landscape photograph credited to ESO/P. Horálek. The source does not publish camera, exposure or color-processing details.
understand.eye: Gegenschein is very faint, and a camera gathering light over time can show it more plainly than the eye usually can.
